important.name: A malformed exclusions file escapes as a traceback from diff_delta.py and from pr-sum
important.summary:
project_patterns (diff_delta.py:72-86) calls load_exclusions, which raises json.JSONDecodeError on bad JSON and KeyError/TypeError on a file without an `exclusions` list of `{pattern}` rows. Neither error is converted. scripts/diff_delta.py:85-91 catches only DeltaError and ConfigError, so a broken file prints a traceback. That contradicts the module docstring (line 14: 'Every failure exits 1 with one problem: ... line on stderr and nothing on stdout'). In the same CLI, an explicit --repo with git missing raises OSError from _root's bare subprocess.run (line 54), and the default path's project_root can raise TimeoutError; both escape the same way. pr-sum never read the exclusions file before this PR. Now PrFile.artifact (pr_summary.py:64-66) reads it through active_patterns, so a malformed file crashes capture/diff/build with a traceback from a property: pr_sum.main (pr_sum.py:441-448) catches only ConfigError and CaptureError. D5 chose 'a summary never fails on a review-only file' for the missing-file case; the malformed case has the opposite outcome.

Also (roast): `project_patterns` calls `load_exclusions`, which raises `json.JSONDecodeError` on bad JSON, `KeyError` when the `exclusions` key or an entry's `pattern` is missing, and `TypeError` on a wrong shape. No caller catches these. In pr-sum the read runs inside the `PrFile.artifact` property (through `active_patterns`), so `capture`, `diff` and `build` all die with a raw traceback, because `pr_sum.main` catches only `ConfigError` and `CaptureError`. Before this PR pr-sum never read that file, so this failure mode is new. `scripts/diff_delta.py` promises in its docstring that every failure exits 1 with one `problem:` line, but it catches only `DeltaError` and `ConfigError`, so the same file breaks that promise. D5 settled the missing-file case and left the corrupt-file case open; a summary tool that crashes on a review-only config file is exactly what D5 meant to prevent.

Also (runtime): `diff_delta.project_patterns` (diff_delta.py:72-86) re-implements `review_plan.exclusion_patterns` (review_plan.py:140-149): the configured file merged with the harness patterns, or empty when `exclusions` is null. They differ when a configured file is missing. The review_plan copy calls load_exclusions, which raises FileNotFoundError, so pr-review capture fails. The diff_delta copy falls back to the harness patterns, so pr-sum and the diff_delta CLI go on. pr_review.plan_scope builds `scope.excluded` (and so `stats.source`) from the review_plan copy, while `PrFile.artifact` on the same PrFacts reads `diff_delta.active_patterns`. The PR shares the predicate (`is_machine_generated`) but not the pattern source, and its docstring (diff_delta.py:5) says one rule is shared.

Also (system_shape): The module docstring (diff_delta.py:5-7) and pr_summary.py:8-9 call this 'one rule shared by pr-review and pr-sum'. The predicate is shared, but the pattern lookup is written twice. diff_delta.project_patterns (diff_delta.py:72-86) repeats review_plan.exclusion_patterns (review_plan.py:140-149): the same null check, the same load_exclusions plus with_harness_patterns call, and the same deferred imports. The only difference is the missing-file fallback that D5 chose. If one copy changes later (a new harness pattern source, a new config key), pr-sum and pr-review will drift apart again, which is the outcome the spec's anti-goal (two definitions of machine-generated) is meant to rule out.

Also (roast): `diff_delta.project_patterns` and `review_plan.exclusion_patterns` repeat the same steps: read `cfg.exclusions`, return `()` when it is null, then `with_harness_patterns(cfg, load_exclusions(repo / cfg.exclusions))`. They differ only in how they handle a missing file (fallback versus raise). The PR's goal was one definition of machine-generated, and it now has two pattern loaders that can drift, for example when the harness patterns change or the configured path gets normalized.
fix: In diff_delta.project_patterns, catch (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) around load_exclusions and raise DeltaError naming the file. In scripts/diff_delta.py, catch OSError (TimeoutError included) in main, and build _root on harness_lib.project.run_git so it gets the timeout. pr-sum then either falls back to harness_patterns(cfg) for a DeltaError, in line with D5, or pr_sum.main catches DeltaError and prints a problem: line. Add a test that writes a malformed exclusions file and asserts exit 1 with one problem: line for both drivers.

In `project_patterns`, wrap the `load_exclusions` call and re-raise `(OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)` as `DeltaError(f"exclusions file {target}: {exc}")`. Add `DeltaError` to the `except` in `pr_sum.main`. Add one test per CLI that writes a malformed exclusions file and asserts exit 1 with a `problem:` line.
Make pr-sum lenient to match D5: on a malformed file `active_patterns` falls back to `harness_patterns(cfg)`, while the CLI still raises `DeltaError`. Pin both paths with tests.

Make `review_plan.exclusion_patterns(repo)` return `diff_delta.project_patterns(repo)`, so one loader feeds both skills. Decide which missing-file behavior is the contract (error or harness-only fallback) and update the pr-review test that pins it.
Or remove `project_patterns` and have diff_delta call `review_plan.exclusion_patterns`, moving the missing-file fallback there.

Keep a single lookup: have review_plan.exclusion_patterns call diff_delta.project_patterns with a strict flag (raise on a missing file), or have project_patterns return harness_patterns(cfg) when the file is missing and otherwise return review_plan.exclusion_patterns(repo).
Move the shared body into one private helper both functions call, with the missing-file policy as a parameter.
Give `project_patterns` a `strict: bool = False` parameter that raises on a missing file, and make `review_plan.exclusion_patterns` return `diff_delta.project_patterns(repo, strict=True)`.

important.name: sweep_hits tracked-file rescan has no regression test
important.summary:
plan_checks.sweep_hits (plan_checks.py:243-269) now runs git grep twice in the working tree: once over tracked files and once with --untracked. The commit message says the rescan is there because --untracked honors ignore rules and dropped a tracked file under an ignored folder. tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py covers untracked files (line 197) but never builds a tracked file under a .gitignore'd folder, so the fix can be reverted or broken (for example, by dropping the first `[]` entry from `runs`) without any test failing. Plan sweeps are a freeze/lint gate, and the git grep ignore semantics behind this fix are subtle enough that a later cleanup could easily undo it.

Also (roast): `sweep_hits` now runs `git grep` twice, once over tracked files and once with `--untracked`, so that a tracked file under an ignored folder is not dropped. This bug fix rides along in the DiffDelta PR, outside every plan task, and no test in `tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py` commits a file under a gitignored folder to show it is found. Nothing stops the next refactor from collapsing the two runs back into one.
fix: Add a test in tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py: make_project with a .gitignore naming `gen/`, write gen/x.txt holding the sweep pattern, `git add -f gen/x.txt`, and assert sweep_hits(root, pattern, 'docs/plans') contains 'gen/x.txt' (and still contains an untracked, non-ignored hit).

Add a test in `tests/lib/test_plan_checks.py`: `make_project`, add an ignored folder to `.gitignore`, force-add and commit a file inside it that matches the pattern, then assert that `sweep_hits(root, pattern, 'docs/plans')` includes it in the working-tree search (`rev=None`).

important.name: diff_delta CLI lets config and git failures escape as tracebacks
important.summary:
The module docstring (scripts/diff_delta.py:14) promises that every failure exits 1 with one `problem: ...` line on stderr. `main` (lines 85-91) catches only DeltaError and ConfigError. Two routes skip that: (1) `between` -> `diff_delta.project_patterns` -> `load_exclusions` raises json.JSONDecodeError on a malformed exclusions file, KeyError when the `exclusions` key is missing and TypeError on a wrong shape, and none of them is wrapped. (2) `_root` (lines 53-54) calls subprocess.run with no try, so a missing git binary raises FileNotFoundError (and with no timeout, unlike `_numstat`). Either way the user gets a Python traceback and exit code 1 from the interpreter instead of the documented problem line.

Also (system_shape): The spec lists the CLI as a goal (2026-11-06-diff-delta-design.md:17) and the plan built it (TASK-2). A search under plugins/ finds 'diff_delta.py' only in the script's own docstring and in pr_review.py's import of the library module. No SKILL.md, operating rule or README tells an agent the command exists or what its status line means. Since agents find harness commands through skill text, the command can only be found by reading the scripts folder.
fix: In harness_lib/diff_delta.py project_patterns, wrap the load_exclusions call: `except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc: raise DeltaError(f"exclusions file {target}: {exc}") from exc`; in scripts/diff_delta.py _root, wrap subprocess.run in `try/except OSError as exc: raise DeltaError(f"--repo {repo}: {exc}") from exc` and pass `timeout=`.
Widen the `except` in scripts/diff_delta.py main to `(DeltaError, ConfigError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)` so every failure prints one problem line.

Add a short entry for `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hpy" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/diff_delta.py" REF_A REF_B [--repo DIR] [--json]` and its status line to the skill that should surface it (pr-sum SKILL.md next to the delta-table paragraph, or merge-commit-msg where the spec's non-goal mentions a later move to DiffDelta.between).

minor.name: from_stats runs the exclusion predicate twice per row
minor.summary: `from_stats` (diff_delta.py:60-62) calls `excluded(s.path)` once to build `kept` and again to build `left_out`. Under `from_patterns`, each call does an fnmatch over every pattern plus a `path_bucket` lookup through the active config, so every file is classified twice.
fix: Classify once: `flags = [(s, excluded(s.path)) for s in rows]`, then `kept = [s for s, x in flags if not x]` and `left_out = tuple(sorted(s.path for s, x in flags if x))`.

minor.name: set_stats keeps a stale stats.source when the totals change
minor.summary:
`set_stats` (review_edit.py:189-198) now copies the existing `stats.source` unchanged while it replaces additions, deletions and files_changed. The review_edit `stats` command exists to correct the totals, for example after new commits. After that correction `source` still holds the old capture's counts, so the document can say source.additions > additions, which contradicts the schema's description of `source` as the same counts without the machine-generated paths. Neither the schema nor set_stats checks this.

Also (overall): review_edit.set_stats (review_edit.py:189-198) copies an existing stats.source unchanged while replacing the totals. The `review_edit.py stats` subcommand (scripts/review_edit.py:115,162-164) has no way to set or clear source, so after `stats 1 0 1` a document can carry source.additions 3 > additions 1. Nothing checks that source is at most the totals, and the document then reports a source count that its own totals contradict.

Also (system_shape): review_edit.set_stats (review_edit.py:189-198) now copies an existing source into the new stats. The `stats ADD DEL FILES` subcommand (scripts/review_edit.py:25,162-164) takes only the three totals and offers no way to set or drop source. After a manual re-stat, for example once the PR has moved to a new head, the document pairs fresh totals with a source taken from the earlier diff. The schema cannot catch source > totals, and neither the usage line nor operating_rules.md:51 says that source survives the edit. The spec chose 'keeps an existing source rather than dropping it', so this is about making that choice visible and recoverable, not reversing it.

Also (roast): `set_stats` resets the three totals and copies any existing `source` across unchanged. If someone lowers the totals (the case `review_edit stats` exists for), the document can end up with `source.additions > additions`. That cannot happen in a real diff, and neither the setter nor the schema rejects it. The design asked to keep `source`, not to keep it when it is impossible.
fix: Keep `source` only when the new totals equal the old ones; otherwise drop it (it is optional in the schema).
Or give set_stats an optional `source` mapping and refuse any source count above its total.
Drop the carried source when any new total is below the matching source count, and add the case to test_pr_review_stats_source.py.
Add optional --source-additions/--source-deletions/--source-files to the stats subcommand so an edit can restate both, and document that a totals-only edit keeps the old source.
Add optional source counts to the `stats` subcommand (e.g. `--source ADD DEL FILES`) that set_stats writes when given, and name it in the scripts/review_edit.py usage docstring.
Have set_stats refuse a kept source whose counts exceed the new totals, so a stale source cannot pass silently.
At minimum, extend the usage line at scripts/review_edit.py:25 and the set_stats docstring to say that an existing source is kept unchanged.
In `set_stats`, raise `ValueError` when a kept `source` count exceeds the matching new total, naming both values. Add a case to `test_set_stats_keeps_an_existing_source`.
Drop the kept `source` when it exceeds the new totals and say so in the docstring.

minor.summary:

By that precedent the additive stats.source is a minor bump (2.2.0). Reviews written with source and reviews written without it now both claim 2.1.0, so the version no longer tells a consumer whether stats.source can be present. The version is mirrored in review_merge.SCHEMA_VERSION and in tests/lib/test_review_merge.py:404, so a bump touches those together. If the project treats the change as too small to bump, the README protocol should say so.

Also (overall): PR_REVIEW.schema.json adds the optional stats.source object (lines 110-136) but $version stays 2.1.0 (line 4), as do review_merge.SCHEMA_VERSION (review_merge.py:53) and the README's 'currently "2.1.0"' (schemas/README.md:31). The README's own precedent (line 33) bumped to 2.1.0 for the optional, non-breaking fix_kind field, so a 2.1.0 document now has two possible stats shapes and no version marks which one it is.

Also (system_shape): schemas/README.md:33 records that 2.1.0 was cut for the optional, non-breaking issue field fix_kind, and README.md:31 says the version is 'currently 2.1.0'. This PR adds the optional stats.source object (PR_REVIEW.schema.json:110-136) but leaves "$version": "2.1.0" (PR_REVIEW.schema.json:4), review_merge.SCHEMA_VERSION = "2.1.0" (review_merge.py:53) and the README version text unchanged. Review JSONs written before and after this change both claim 2.1.0, so a reader cannot tell from the version whether stats.source can be present. The README's 'Version bump protocol' paragraph also does not mention stats.source.

Also (roast): `PR_REVIEW.schema.json` gains the optional `stats.source` object, but `$version` stays at `2.1.0`. The README's bump protocol cites `2.1.0` as the minor bump for the optional `fix_kind` field, so an additive optional field has precedent for a minor bump. As it stands, review JSONs with and without `source` both claim the same version.

Also (docs): schemas/README.md:31-33 records `2.1.0` as the bump for the optional issue field `fix_kind` (non-breaking). This PR adds another optional field, `stats.source`, yet the schema `$version` (PR_REVIEW.schema.json:4), review_merge.SCHEMA_VERSION (review_merge.py:53) and the README 'currently "2.1.0"' line stay at 2.1.0, so review JSONs with and without `source` carry the same version and the README's version history skips the change. minor.name: stats.source description leaves out the harness output patterns that the shared rule applies
minor.summary: The machine-generated rule is the project's exclusions file, plus the harness output patterns that with_harness_patterns adds in memory when the file lacks them (default_exclusions.py:60-67), plus the Artifact commit bucket. diff_delta.py:5-7, scripts/diff_delta.py:7-8, pr_summary.py:8-9 and pr-sum SKILL.md:89-90 name all three parts. The schema description (PR_REVIEW.schema.json:112), schemas/README.md:35 and the PrFile.artifact docstring (pr_summary.py:65) name only 'the exclusions file and the Artifact commit bucket'. A project whose own exclusions file omits docs/PR_REVIEWS/* still has those paths dropped from stats.source, which these three texts do not say.
fix: Change all three to name the harness output patterns: e.g. 'the project's exclusions file, the harness output patterns and the Artifact commit bucket' in PR_REVIEW.schema.json:112 and schemas/README.md:35, and 'an exclusions-file or harness output pattern, or the Artifact commit bucket' in pr_summary.py:65.

No sections.', but render_summary inserts the Source / Machine-generated / Total delta table right after the Summary at every level whenever a file is machine-generated (pr_summary.py:579-587, delta_table at 494-507). A reader of the Levels table gets an incomplete list of what a level 1 summary holds, which disagrees with the Step 1 paragraph at lines 89-92.

Add one line under the Levels table: 'Every level adds the delta table under the Summary when any file is machine-generated.'

minor.name: Three docs state the machine-generated rule three different ways
minor.summary:
The code rule (diff_delta.project_patterns plus is_machine_generated, and review_plan.exclusion_patterns for pr-review) is: the configured exclusions file merged with the harness output patterns, or the Artifact commit bucket; with `exclusions: null` both pattern sources drop out and only Artifact applies. pr-sum SKILL.md:89-90 lists the harness output patterns as a peer alternative to the exclusions file, which reads as if they apply when `exclusions` is null (project_patterns returns () then, diff_delta.py:81-82). schemas/README.md:35 and the PR_REVIEW.schema.json stats.source description (line 112) go the other way and name only the exclusions file and the Artifact bucket, omitting the harness output patterns that pr-review's exclusion_patterns adds (review_plan.py:147-149). The diff_delta.py module docstring (lines 5-7) has the accurate wording.

Also (skill_package): SKILL.md:89-90 says machine-generated files are paths matching the project's exclusions file or the harness output patterns, or classified as Artifact. In code, active_patterns and project_patterns return () when the exclusions key is null (diff_delta.py:81-82, 103-104), so the harness output patterns are dropped too and only the Artifact bucket applies. A project with exclusions set to null gets reviews, summaries and scratch files counted as Source, contrary to the prose.

Also (roast): `scripts/diff_delta.py` is one of the spec's four goals, yet no SKILL.md, agent file or README mentions it. It is named only in the spec and the plan, so in practice the command has no users unless someone reads `scripts/`.
fix: Align the three texts on the diff_delta.py docstring wording: SKILL.md:89-90 'paths matching the project's `exclusions` file (plus the harness output patterns), or classified as Artifact by the commit buckets'; schemas/README.md:35 and PR_REVIEW.schema.json:112 '(the project's exclusions file plus the harness output patterns, and the Artifact commit bucket)'.
Reword to: 'paths matching the project's exclusions file and the harness output patterns (both off when exclusions is null), or classified as Artifact by the commit buckets'
Or make active_patterns return harness_patterns(cfg) when exclusions is null, if the prose states the intended rule (a design choice shared with pr-review)

Add a short line with the `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hpy" "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/diff_delta.py" REF_A REF_B [--json]` invocation to the pr-sum SKILL.md next to the delta-table paragraph, or to the harness plugin README.

minor.name: Module docstring claims every test activates a project
minor.summary:
The module docstring of tests/lib/test_diff_delta.py says every test builds a throwaway project with make_project and activates its configuration. Five tests (test_from_stats_splits_source_and_full, test_nothing_excluded_keeps_equal_counts, test_excluded_paths_are_sorted, test_delta_is_frozen, test_delta_payload_shape) take no make_project fixture and activate nothing; they pass lambda predicates to from_stats and never reach the configuration.

Also (tests): active_patterns() documents 'reread only when its exclusions file changes' (diff_delta.py:99), keyed on mtime_ns and size. test_active_patterns_follow_the_file_on_disk only checks that a rewritten file is picked up, and the rewrite changes the file size, so an implementation that rereads on every call passes, and one that ignored mtime (size-only key) passes too. The caching half of the contract is unpinned.
fix: Reword lines 4-5 to: 'Every test that reads the machine-generated rule or the project patterns builds a throwaway project with ``make_project`` and activates its configuration; the pure from_stats tests pass a predicate and read no configuration.'

Add `assert active_patterns() is active_patterns()` before the rewrite (same cached tuple object), and add a second rewrite with equal byte length plus os.utime(path, ns=(t, t + 10**9)) that asserts the new pattern appears, pinning the mtime half of the key.

minor.name: Delta table sign formatting tested only for positive nets
minor.summary: _delta_rows renders Net with f'{adds - subs:+d}', so a net-deletion PR shows '-N' and a balanced row shows '+0'. Every table test in tests/lib/test_pr_summary_delta.py uses rows with positive nets (+2, +40, +42), so the negative and zero cases, the common shape of a cleanup PR, are unpinned.
fix: Add a test with PrFile('M', 'src/pkg/a.py', None, 1, 5) and PrFile('A', 'gen/out.json', None, 2, 2) asserting the Source row ends '|  -4 |' and the Machine-generated row ends '|  +0 |' (or pin the full table text as _TABLE does).
